verses.english: Linked Discourses 12.58
6. A Tree
Name and Form
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: “Saṁyojaniyesu, bhikkhave, dhammesu assādānupassino viharato nāmarūpassa avakkanti hoti.
verses.english: “There are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, name and form are conceived.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
Suppose there was a great tree.

verses.pali: Tassa yāni ceva mūlāni adhogamāni, yāni ca tiriyaṅgamāni, sabbāni tāni uddhaṁ ojaṁ abhiharanti.
verses.english: And its roots going downwards and across all draw the sap upwards.

verses.pali: Evañhi so, bhikkhave, mahārukkho tadāhāro tadupādāno ciraṁ dīghamaddhānaṁ tiṭṭheyya.
verses.english: Fed and fuelled by that, the great tree would stand for a long time.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, saṁyojaniyesu dhammesu assādānupassino viharato nāmarūpassa avakkanti hoti …pe….
verses.english: In the same way, there are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, name and form are conceived. …

verses.pali: Saṁyojaniyesu, bhikkhave, dhammesu ādīnavānupassino viharato nāmarūpassa avakkanti na hoti.
verses.english: There are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, name and form are not conceived.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
Suppose there was a great tree.
Then a person comes along with a spade and basket. …
In this way the great tree is cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, saṁyojaniyesu dhammesu ādīnavānupassino viharato nāmarūpassa avakkanti na hoti.
verses.english: In the same way, there are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, name and form are not conceived.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
